slots.name: degree rate
slots.sentence: A survey of Michigan foster youth over a four-year period, part of a national assessment, found that only about 1% earned a postsecondary degree – bachelor’s or associate’s – by their 21st birthday. The number who reported being enrolled in school decreased from 93% at age 17 to 26% at age 21.

slots.name: homeless rate
slots.sentence: Nineteen percent of the 19-year-olds surveyed for the National Youth in Transition Database — the same survey that found Michigan’s grad rates for foster youth are lower than the national average — reported that they had been homeless at some point over the prior two years. The rate was 24% for 17-year-olds and 16% for those 21.

slots.name: national degree rate
slots.sentence: Nationally, researchers have found that only about 10% of people who spent time in foster care received a two- or four-year degree by their mid- to late 20s, a rate that’s five times lower than the general population.
